subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which staged product/security boundary should OpenClaw support first from this RFC: capability-aware routing, a shared-memory/blackboard API, token-budget enforcement, or a narrower meeting/teleconference primitive?
rationale: The current code has lower-level primitives but the requested four-layer stack crosses core/plugin boundaries, persisted state, memory visibility, config, delegation authority, and budget enforcement, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Stage the RFC into API/security phases
options.body: Keep #35203 open as the design anchor, define storage and authorization contracts, then implement one narrow phase at a time.

options.title: Route first to teleconference work
options.body: Use #65403 as the first concrete on-ramp and defer blackboard, learned profiles, and budget governance until that primitive lands or is rejected.

options.title: Reject heavy orchestration for now
options.body: Close the broad core RFC as outside current vision and invite narrower plugin/API-gap proposals instead.

recommendation.title: Stage the RFC into API/security phases
recommendation.body: Keep #35203 open as the design anchor, define storage and authorization contracts, then implement one narrow phase at a time.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from recent agent capability/tool-policy history and multi-agent scoping discussion.
